Q: Base language for programming language experimentation A:

I'm requesting this question be deleted for two reasons.

I had asked this question in a good-faith attempt to get a quality answer from the opinion-based question experiment. This really is a question I'm interested in, and I'd hoped it'd get more interesting answers than, say, "what are some good open-source AI libraries?"

With thanks to the two people who did leave replies, this hasn't gotten the answer I'd hoped for. I'd love to have found an answer based around LLVM. I did in fact spend a couple of weeks playing with a Forth interpreter in Rust, and got much further in Rust than I had before. But that's not a base for the sorts of syntax experiments I wanted to play with.

Watching the meta discussion about the site redesign leaves me unconvinced a good-faith attempt to use the experimental UI is actually valuable, or that my feedback will be listened to. I've been advising people on other questions to always pick the "troubleshooting" question type because of the major unresolved bugs in the experimental UI.

If the experimental UI is so broken that I'm recommending that nobody uses it, then I shouldn't use it myself either. If I don't want to use the experimental UI, then this question is off-topic because it's asking for a recommendation and it should be closed.

Q: Code Helper process by VS Code eating my cpu A:

SOLUTION (MAC ARM CHIPS)

Problem is that you are running INTEL version, you need to download the ARM version. Once you do that, all the problems go away. You can verify this with Activity Monitor, you will see process is a INTEL process (column to the right) running on a MAC AMD chip).
